subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — GPU / TPS / concurrency / token mix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Sullivan <kate@fintech.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — GPU / TPS / concurrency / token mix

Hi Kate — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated properly for FinTech.io.

Recap (from our conversation):
- Primary workload: interactive chat + multi-turn ticket summarization and categorization.
- Model preference: leaning toward an open LLM (e.g., Llama 3 / mix) but you want Redwood to recommend optimal model variants.
- Deployment need: dedicated GPU pool (predictable throughput & data isolation). Considering Private VPC later.

Sizing questions we need to lock down:
1) Target TPS (requests per second) or peak concurrent requests you expect (p95 and burst).
2) Average and peak token mix: prompt tokens vs response tokens; typical prompt length and expected average response length.
3) Expected concurrency per request (how many parallel conversations per user session, if any).
4) Desired P95 latency SLA (e.g., <150ms for short prompts, or <500ms typical).
5) Preferred GPU family (A100, H100, L4) or if you'd like our cost-optimized recommendation.

I've attached a short workbook (dedicated-sizing-workbook.xlsx) — please fill in the highlighted cells for TPS and token mix. If it's easier, paste the numbers into a reply and we'll do the math on our side.

Next steps:
- You fill/confirm TPS and token mix OR we schedule a 30-min technical sizing with Aditya/Rafael.
- We’ll produce a recommended capacity plan (GPU types, nodes, concurrency settings, estimated monthly cost) and an optional canary rollout plan.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

From: Kate Sullivan <kate@fintech.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fintech.io>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — GPU / TPS / concurrency / token mix

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- TPS: our baseline for production is ~30 TPS sustained across the US (active users during market hours). We expect bursts up to ~120 TPS for a few minutes around peak events.
- Concurrent sessions: roughly 200 concurrent active conversations at peak (concurrency per user is 1).
- Token mix: average prompt ~120 tokens, average response ~180 tokens. About 75% of requests are short prompts (~<100 tokens) and 25% are longer summarization jobs (~>512 tokens).
- Latency: target p95 generation latency under 400ms is ideal; p99 under 750ms would be helpful but not a hard requirement for launch.
- GPUs: cost-sensitive — we'd prefer cost-effective GPUs unless we need H100 for specific latency SLAs. Open to your recommendation.

I'll route the workbook to Tom (ops) to fill in traffic seasonality and burst windows.

Cheers,
Kate Sullivan
Head of Integrations, FinTech.io
kate@fintech.io

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Sullivan <kate@fintech.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — Dedicated capacity sizing proposal request

Thanks Kate — that's super helpful. Rafael/Aditya, looping you in to propose an initial config based on FinTech.io's numbers: sustained 30 TPS, peaks to 120 TPS, ~200 concurrent sessions, token mix (avg prompt 120 / avg resp 180, 25% long jobs).

Initial sizing notes (high-level):
- Model family assumption: optimized Llama-3-ish 70B quantized variant for cost/quality balance; can recommend alternatives.
- GPU options:
  - L4: best price-per-token for mostly short requests; may hit latency targets for short prompts, but struggles on long summarization jobs.
  - A100 80GB: solid middle ground — good for mix workloads and batching; supports larger sequence lengths.
  - H100: best p99/p95 latency for high-concurrency low-latency SLAs but higher cost.
- Concurrency/batching: given 30 TPS sustained, we'll likely configure continuous batching with target batch window ~20–40ms to optimize throughput while keeping p95 under target. For bursts, autoscaling with pre-warmed nodes is recommended.

Action items:
- Rafael/Aditya: can you run quick capacity calc (nodes of each GPU type, expected token/sec, estimated p95) and return with two configurations: cost-optimized (L4/A100 mix) and low-latency (A100/H100) with estimated monthly cost?
- Kate/Tom: once we have the two configs we can pick and schedule a 45-min technical runbook session to agree canary and autoscale strategy.

I attached Redwood's Dedicated T&Cs and the workbook again. Rafael — any extra telemetry we should ask FinTech.io to provide (seq length distribution, peak window hour-of-day) before sizing final?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Sullivan <kate@fintech.io>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fintech.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — Dedicated capacity sizing proposal request

Thanks Marissa / Kate — quick follow-up from the infra side. I'll run the node-level calc today and have two configs by EOD:

Some immediate asks to make numbers tighter:
- Can you provide 1 week of production-like traffic (CSV) with timestamped request sizes (prompt tokens + response tokens) and a flag for long jobs? If you can't share production data, a sampled day is fine.
- What percentage of requests require tool-calls or function-calling (these increase latency and token consumption)?
- Do you expect multi-model routing (e.g., routing long summarization jobs to a larger/cheaper model variant)?

Preliminary guidance: with 30 sustained TPS and your token mix, starting point is:
- Cost-optimized: 8 x L4 nodes (with batching + prefix caching) able to handle 30 sustained TPS and short bursts, plus autoscale buffer to reach 120 TPS. Estimated baseline performance: p95 ~350–500ms on average short prompts; long jobs will have higher variance.
- Low-latency: 6 x A100 80GB (or 4 x H100) configured with lower batch window and larger pre-warmed pool to hit p95 <250–350ms for typical prompts and much better p99.

I'll include estimated monthly cost, estimated token/sec per node, and a suggested autoscaling policy (scale steps, warm nodes) in my note.

Happy to schedule a tech deep-dive tomorrow with Aditya if that helps lock in telemetry and deployment preferences.

—Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
